item.title: Omelette of Misfortunate Death
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): OMELETTE

Elevator Pitch:
An omelette is discovered. Delicious. Many guards and researchers at the foundation go mad over this beautiful omelette.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
An omelette is discovered on the top of a statue, in the middle of a small town, in Oregon. People begin going mad for omelettes around the area. People begin dying due to over omeletting. A threat is posed. Anyone who sees the omelette becomes crazed with trying to recreated an omelette just as beautiful. No one who tries succeeds. They become mad with failure. Their brains become scrambled. What must they do to create the perfect Omelette without dying? The foundation becomes involved after a whole town dies of starvation with in a matter of days. The town had an ample food source. How did they die with all the omelettes? The source they find is this SCP. The foundation takes the omelette into confinement. They begin tests and find several interesting facts about the omelette, such as, it does not decompose. They begin to question whether or not its sentient. Many misfortunate tests happen until researchers at the foundation finally find a good use for this SCP.

Attention Getter:
Is the Omelette sentient? It's a Omelette for peat sakes, that at least sparks my attention. Will the omelette take over the world if it escapes or will it plunge everyone around it into immediate cooking failures and death?
Additional notes:
I am currently waiting on my original SCP idea to be critiqued so I decided to add another strange idea. I am new and again no matter how harsh, I would still enjoy criticism!

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who conducted a battery of tests on him to see how different causes of death would affect him.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This kid isn't any stronger than a normal child, and he can be killed just the same, but nothing will keep him down permanently, even if it takes months for him to recover.

Central Narrative: The different ways the foundation killed him. They've starved him, kept him up for a few months, froze him, burned him, cut him up, poisoned him, introduced him to other Scps such as 053 and 049, and even given him a dish containing shrimp, only to realize he's deathly allergic to the stuff when he went into anaphylactic shock.

But no matter what happens, he'll come back. Often times he's confused or frightened or just plain pissed, but alive and free of any fatal wounds nonetheless. All these tests have left him traumatized, possibly beyond repair.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He can't be killed permanently, at least not in any way that the foundation has discovered.

Additional Notes: The 5091 number is a placeholder, I'll give it another number when I post it to the mainsite.

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Some additional thoughts for you
– hide block

I do have to admit, once i finished the writing i read it about fifty times and every time there’s something that felt out of place or unnecessary but I didn’t know how to approach it. ( got scared to trim it.)

IMO: just trim it.

The central core or what i’m really trying to say through the article would be learning who you really are or having peace with you inner conflict and finding power from it. Once the inner peace is achieved no one can really stop you or tell you that your wrong, but the society as a whole always finds a loop hole on the idea. So I guess i didn’t really made it clear.

I think the central problem with the article, in terms of achieving this at the moment, is that this journey to find peace with your inner conflict isn't actually what the story is about? Like, the Foundation swoops in after it happens, so this like, intimate, personal struggle isn't shown; and instead we have this kinda, overview of what happened as a result of it happening?

My suggestion would be to do one of two things: either make this a tale, or start this sooner in the story.

In the first, you'd be radically changing the PoV so it'd be from SCP-XXXX-1's perspective, and entirely centred around them being put in a place where they're forced to find the peace within them, or in a place where finding that peace is their entire struggle, and the story would unfold as they gradually begin to find it while stuff around them gets worse; and the resolution would likely be when the Foundation comes in an interferes or something.

In the second, the focus would be the Foundation locking up -1 just as he's starting to gain this inner power, and so the central conflict would be around this boy trying to achieve the peace he needs whilst the Foundation are doing everything that they can to stop it: the ending would likely be the boy escaping to form the cave and the peaceful area, instead of that being the start. Like pacing would probably look something like "Foundation grabs minor reality bender; reality bender gets stronger; Foundation does stuff to try and stop this; bender keeps getting more powerful; bender escapes and creates a place of peace, as a mirror to the place of conflict that was the foundation for him".

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: {Redacted}
item.content:encoded:
My thoughts - Note: I am not an experienced reviewer, and cannot give greenlights.

+ Show
- Hide

I hope it hasn't been done before.

Unfortunately, this idea has been done before - notably in SCP-055, but also in SCP-579 and SCP-5790. The idea of an anomaly with information being anomalously hard to gain is already called 'antimemetics' - a pretty well-explored concept on the wiki - but that doesn't mean a concept like this wouldn't work. For starters, expand your concept. It's hard to review a story without elaboration on the storyline, as even a bland anomaly can have an interesting storyline. Secondly, see what works in other antimemetic articles. In the articles I gave, its the information they do have, not the information they don't, that makes them interesting - the use of bizarre containment procedures hint at a threat that cant be talked about, and so on. I wouldn't recommend doing these formulas exactly, but try and do something interesting with the concept of a self-redacting anomaly. Finally; if you are gonna go down a comedic route, I just don't think 'so what is it?' will work very well, as the idea has already been used seriously a ton, so it doesn't mesh well, for experienced readers - but that's just my opinion. If you revise this idea, feel free to PM me, and I'll look over it again.

Hope that helps!

There are some questions it should answer:

Does the entity behaves the same, as if part of the video, or does it change in behaviour each time?

How does the affected subject reacts to the video throughout it? The description says only the subject orgasms at the end, but the sample occurrences imply unconsciousness and something else far before the end.

Why isn't there some tests to show what happens to subjects during the video? And why they didn't try to contain the entity instead of harming it?

In particular for the later paragraph describing it as just acquired and the shooting as accidental, unavoidable or done by a third party would help to reconcile the story with the idea of it being at Foundation custody now.

For now, downvoted.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

Playing with Fire - silly putty like substance that is plasma at room temperature, from Dr. Wondertainment.
Vampire Bodega - mini-mart where everything seems to be free, but actually draws blood from customers, not noticeable unless the customer comes more than twice a week. May be part of Marshall, Carter and Dark.
Cryovampire - cryogenically preserved person who was successfully revived, but now absorbs heat energy. Must be kept in a room heated to 98.6 degrees Farenheit at which point the ambient temperature neutralizes the anomaly, but as soon as it is exposed to lower temperatures it reverts to a savage that freezes anything it touches.
Alzoidian - a cephalopod like alien life form native to the red spot of Jupiter. Exists in symbiosis with a fungus and another species that resembles a manta ray. Still not quite sure how to explain how the foundation even acquired it…
Scapegoats - the cursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.
Swine Legion - the cursed swine possessed by demons exorcised by Jesus.

SPC-2806: cybernetics for pugilists who lost limbs in shark attacks so that they may once again punch sharks.

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea for a character that I have a lot of confidence in, but I want to make sure I introduce him correctly. First impressions matter, and if I do this wrong, it could be the end for him, and maybe me too.

So the idea is a cyborg, but not really a complex cyborg, actually he just has a cybernetic arm. It's a concept I have worked with a lot, and I feel it could work with SCP-2806. I know I could make up something more original, but that entry felt like it had everything I needed to work with and I want to work with the universe rather than forcing it around me. The long term story is that he ends up in Alpha-9, but not because he's the coolest guy in the room, but because he got into a situation where he got the offer and it was either this or amnestics, and frankly it was enough on the edge the Foundation was cool either way. So the interesting part of the story is that this a guy who's saving the world one skip at a time because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Where I'm at I think it would work to edit the original article adding the new instance to the description, adding a new containment procedure for the new instance, and an interview between the agent and the SCP to get some info on what seperated this guy from all the others that just get the Skywalker protocol. Should I do all that, or just post the interview as it's own tale with a reference to the article?

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hey all. My name's John, and I'm a teenager living in Michigan, USA.

I've known about the Foundation for years now, and it's been long enough that I don't remember exactly how I discovered it, although it was probably through watching Let's Plays of Containment Breach back in the day. This community seems like a welcoming place, but I'm not quite sure what I want to do here, whether it be writing SCPs or just reading and giving my input.

In real life, I like learning about history and government, and just researching things in general. More recently, I've started to get into graphic design and perhaps even architecture, which seems like a good career to go into.

What keeps me up at night is mostly my imagination. I usually either place myself in fictional scenarios, or use fictional characters to carry out said scenarios. These scenarios I create usually revolve around something that interests me or whatever occupied my time that day. Hopefully I can utilize my creativity and put it to good use here.

I'm glad to be finally joining the site after all these years, and I'm looking forward to contributing to the community.

item.title: SCP Idea green light
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Elevator Pitch: 4 unseen ancient lineages of nautiloids are found around the Atlantic Ocean. Each one is drastically different from the other. Not only in physiology, but also in tactics, weapons, and speed.
Though they rarely interact, every five years, one individual from each of these nautiloid lineages will travel to the center of the Bermuda Triangle. After each battle, only one individual will leave the deathmatch.

Central Narrative: Four undiscovered nautiloids species were discovered fighting in the middle of the Bermuda Triangle by an international oceanography survey. They were later discovered in different parts of the Atlantics with little overlap in population overlap.

SCP-XXXX-A are conical-shelled nautiloids resembling Orthoceras in physique. Shell length is 4 meters. The arm length is 1.5 meters each arm. Skin is red with a brown shell. During Autumn, the instances of SCP-XXXX-a will migrate to the southern Atlantic until mid-April.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-B are curved-shelled nautiloids living in the Caribbean. Shell length of the instance is 1.5 meters. A protrusion of iron from a meter up extends 20cm out from the shell. Arms of this instance are a meter long and hooked. Webbing is present between the arms 20cm from the base.

SCP-XXXX-C has a shell diameter of 1 meter. Resembling a form of a modern nautilus. Grooves are present where the walls of the air chambers are located. Skin is mostly navy blue.

SCP-XXXX-D are coiled-shelled nautiloids with a shell diameter of 2 meters. The shell is a gradient of orange and yellow with a black rock outer layer on it. Arms of SCP-XXXX-D instance are retracted and have microscopic hairs. Arms extend to 5 meters when in use.

Every 10 years, a ritual of fertility will be held by each instance of SCP-XXXX at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The ritual ends until the last instance is alive. The sole survivor of the ritual, for example, an instance of SCP-XXXX-B, will have a population boom of three years for its instance.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humans know more of what’s above them than what’s below the deep oceans. The oceans are scary indeed. About 90-97% of the ocean is still undiscovered. The ocean is the last frontier to travel on this planet. Many creatures are left undiscovered to this day.

Additional Notes: Draft is almost complete. Sketches of the entities will come soon.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Licensing Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
A good thing to keep in mind is how easily you can swap this out with a similar brand/song, and retain a cohesive article. Say you write an SCP loosely surrounding "Hit Me With Your Best Shot." If you can swap that song out with "God Save the Queen," and not have any significant impact on your article, that is considered acceptable. Likewise, if your narrative involves a Macy's but can be replaced with a 99 cent store, that is acceptable as well.

Bear in mind if you do end up referencing a song, it's better to err on the safe side and just note who wrote the song in your author post. If you intend on using song lyrics, however, the situation becomes significantly more complicated and you will have to do your own research on whether the lyrics are still copyrighted or not.

item.title: Honey, I Shrunk the MTF
item.content:encoded:
Private Lang, Private Pimm

I see what you did there.

Overall, this is goofy and requires some serious suspension of disbelief, but I found it enjoyable nonetheless. +1 because I'm a sucker for camp.

+ Problems with shrinking
- But I'm sure you already knew that

All units (both human and vehicular) of SCP-3198 have been reduced dramatically to a ratio of approximately 1:64 of their original size with a similar reduction in mass.

Let's assume a height of six feet (72 inches), and a weight of 180 lbs. Some quick division tells us that such a person in this situation would be only one and an eighth inches tall, but nearly three pounds in weight. At such a density, I find it unlikely that anything the MTF members come across would be able to do them significant harm (with the exception of poisons like the pesticide spray).

Even falling from the truck as it's picked up by a "giant" wouldn't be enough to kill them. Yes, proportionally, it's like falling from a tall building. But that's not how you calculate the force from a fall. It all comes down to mass and acceleration from gravity. I thought about going into the math for this, but for the sake of brevity, let it suffice to say that two objects of any size, with the same mass, falling from the same height, will hit the ground with the same amount of force. So a normal sized human and a shrunken human with the same mass, falling from the height of one meter, would experience the same amount of force. A shrunken human with diminished mass falling from one meter would experience diminished force by comparison. And considering the density of the shrunken humans in this situation, they'd be more than tough enough to survive that fall.

Related to that, assuming that the helicopter is still capable of flight at that density, it would chop through any birds that tried to attack it. Unless seagulls have wire cutters for beaks, they're not breaking any part of that chopper. Maybe if one fell on top of it, kamikaze style, it could stop up the blades enough to make it fall. But then it's still only actually falling three or four storeys. I'm not super sure on the survivability here, but my gut says it's more than you might first imagine.

Finally, and perhaps most significantly to the plot, there's actually a legitimate reason why the tiny MTF would have difficulty communicating with the Foundation and perceiving the world around them. This idea was introduced to me years ago in a book called "The Science of Superheroes", and it's a great read that I'd highly recommend. Basically, if a human shrunk down to the size of a bug, their eyes would be too small to take in light the way they're supposed to. The book also discussed how hearing would be affected, but I don't remember what it said. The end result though is that the MTF actually wouldn't be able to effectively communicate with the Foundation, or possibly even read the word "Jenga" written in (relatively) large letters. So you actually got that part right!… Except that they would have similar difficulty perceiving themselves and each other, and would definitely not be able to read text messages, or tiny words on paper.

Oh yeah, and that pesky square-cube law means that they'd all lack the surface area required to release body heat, so they'd develop a fever and die in… I dunno, a few minutes?

item.title: SCP Idea Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Page Layout: Basically just a more traditional SCP article, explaining what the anomaly is and what it does in a clinical tone.

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly is a YouTube upload of Gas Gas Gas by Manuel, well known as part of the soundtrack for Initial D. It is one of the most popular uploads of the song on the site. When this upload of the song is played in a motor vehicle, all surrounding vehicles will slow to 1-5 mph (1.6-8.0km/h) under the speed limit. The drivers of these vehicles will not notice their collective decrease in speed, according to foundation research. If the listener makes an attempt to pass on the shoulder or weave around these slower vehicles, law enforcement intervention will occur approximately 83% of the time, regardless of normal police presence. If the listener makes an attempt to evade law enforcement, an auto accident will result approximately 96% of the time. After the song ends, surrounding vehicles will return to normal speed and the probability of police intervention returns to normal, but if a chase ensued during the duration of the song, the risk of auto accident will not decrease.

Central Narrative: There was a debate among researchers whether or not to attempt to contain this SCP. On one hand, a majority of those affected drove more safely during the duration of the song, however, arguments could be easily made that the anomaly was the cause of multiple automotive deaths.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The person affected by the SCP is in full control of what happens as a result. Those prone to anger issues/road rage will be much more likely to be pulled over, arrested, or to die as a result of this anomaly.

Additional Notes: This is me trying to make something serious but also based on a relatively classic meme.

item.title: Re: SCP-The Mimic
item.content:encoded:
+ Crit
– hide block

The SCP is a humanoid entity similar to SCP-096, being tall, disproportionate, and skinny

If you're describing your anomaly as similar to another one, especially one so popular, it's likely to feel overly similar to your readers as well.

SCPs that are scary monsters and not much else have a hard time on the site these days, since they were done so much back in series 1 a decade ago. Generally successful articles nowadays tell a story, using the anomaly as a vessel to tell it. While this does have a vague narrative in here, it has a few glaring issues:

The go crazy a few hours after seeing the image or video, and kill any living thing they see, but can't die themselves.

Things that make you go crazy and things which induce a 'rage state' are two of the most overdone and generally unpopular tropes on the site and would really struggle to survive without bringing something completely new to the table.

it's an endless maze of houses and shops, some buildings being made of obscure materials, including glass, wires, and human components

Additionally, endless dimensions have been done quite a few times before, most notably in SCP-3008, which survives more from its journal than from the actual anomaly.

Overall, this has the problem that both components of it have been done in several other articles, and generally done better. The lack of any story beyond it having killed a village (something which isn't very exciting for a reader, as there's nothing special about reading a clinical description stating that some people died), doesn't help to alleviate these issues. I'd probably recommend considering other ideas here, and will link some guides that might help you in the future. I also recommend you read some more recent articles from Series 5 and Series 6 to get an idea of what works on the site now.
